title: Clap your hands and fireworks appear

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Clap your hands in front of a sensor and fireworks burst on screen. Raise a hand and bubbles float up. That's the sketch Antoine built for a creative-coding class.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How does the computer know you clapped?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A Kinect v2 camera tracks your body as a skeleton of twenty-five joints. A tool called Kinectron streams those joints into the browser, where p5 dot js draws each joint as a dot.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So it's like a stick figure made of dots.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. And every frame, the sketch asks six simple questions: are the hands clapping, is the hand above the hips, are both hands above the head, and so on. Each question is a tiny function that compares joint positions.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What does clapping look like to a computer?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Just distance. Positions come in as numbers between zero and one, so when the two hands get closer than a small fraction of the frame, that's a clap, and fifty firework particles pop out at the right hand.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A hand above the hips releases bubbles that rise. A hand below sends stars falling. The sketch even prints the names of the gestures it detects at the top of the canvas, which makes a great live demo.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a recorded mode. The sketch replays a saved skeleton file frame by frame, and adds Stop and Play buttons, so you can demo it anywhere.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One button calls saveGif, which records five seconds of the canvas and downloads it as a GIF. Perfect for sharing a class project.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I heard something about a smart device.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A fun side experiment. A clap can send a request to a small Node server that uses a library called tuyapi to switch a smart device on the local network on or off. Clap on, clap off.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Skeleton data plus a handful of simple rules gets you an interactive piece quickly. The full tutorial has every step and the code.
